incidents.cause: The student pilot's improper flare resulting in a bounced landing.
The pilot's failure to maintain clearance from an object while taxiing.  Contributing to the accident were the pilot's diverted attention and a vehicle.
The student pilots improper short field landing procedure and excessive rate of descent.  A contributing factor was the student pilots improper recovery from a bounced landing.
The pilot's failure to maintain airspeed during the landing flare which resulted in a hard landing.

The pilot’s decision to takeoff from a contaminated runway with unfavorable wind conditions, and his failure to maintain airspeed during the initial climb, which resulted in an aerodynamic stall. Contributing to the accident was the operator’s inadequate procedures for operational control and dispat
The pilot’s unstabilized approach and a subsequent runway overrun while landing on a short runway in variable wind conditions.

The pilot's unfamiliarity with the airport environment, which resulted in his taxiing the airplane onto a no-taxi section of roadway and into a road sign. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's failure to avail himself of additional information that described the appropriate taxi routes on the
The pilot's selection of unsuitable terrain for landing.
The pilot's decision to land on a short, icy runway with poor braking action, resulting in a runway overrun/excursion and collision with a snowbank.
The student pilot's failure to maintain directional control during the takeoff roll.

The pilot’s failure to adequate clearance from obstacles while maneuvering during the landing approach and the instructor pilot’s delayed remedial action, which resulted in the airplane contacting a tree and terrain.
A total loss of engine power due to oil starvation for undetermined reasons.
The pilot's failure to maintain lateral position in relation to the instrument approach course at night in instrument meteorological conditions, which resulted in collision with a tree.

The pilot’s failure to maintain clearance from power lines during an aerial application flight. Contributing to the accident was the pilot’s cell phone use and the position of the sun, which reduced the pilot’s ability to perceive the location of the power lines.
The pilot’s loss of airplane control resulting in an aerodynamic stall while executing a steep turnaround during an aerial application flight.
The pilot’s failure to maintain clearance from a power line during the spray pass.
The total loss of engine power due to the failure and disengagement of the torque sensor assembly front spur gear from its splined shouldered shaft due to a loose self-locking nut.
An inflight loss of control and subsequent impact with terrain during an aerial application flight for reasons that could not be determined based on the available evidence.
